title: DCLab Watch: DCLab's own spans sent to MLflow and a local Langfuse as OpenTelemetry traces, and its model trainings as MLflow runs
request: The owner asked for tracing and tracking of DCLab, its agents, LLMs and multi-agent team, with Langfuse and MLflow both, the code ready even before Docker runs.
spec: Every request, job, agent run, agent step, tool call and model request already had a W3C trace and span id; each becomes an OpenTelemetry span with those ids, a name, and its names and numbers (model, tokens, euro, seconds, verdict), sent in batches to the targets DCLAB_TRACE_EXPORT names; nothing by default; never a table cell, a prompt, an answer or a sealed span; a target that is down never slows or breaks DCLab; trainings and bench runs as MLflow runs.
plan: the exporter: allowed keys only, a bounded queue, protobuf with DCLab's ids, both targets
name the existing spans and let a span be annotated while it runs
the model request's numbers on its span; the request as the root span
MLflow runs from model cards and bench runs through its REST interface
the scripts and the Langfuse override for this Mac

decisions.decision: Send DCLab's own spans with their own ids rather than a second tracing library's
decisions.why: the ids already join events, logs and the experience record; one trace id everywhere

decisions.decision: An allow-list of attribute keys and short values, nothing else
decisions.why: a viewer outside DCLab's records must never receive a table cell, a prompt or a person's words

decisions.decision: MLflow through its REST interface, no MLflow package in DCLab
decisions.why: the server runs with uvx; DCLab stays light and its dependencies unchanged

decisions.decision: Langfuse runs on demand, its database on 5433 and every port on this machine
decisions.why: this Mac has 8 GB and DCLab's PostgreSQL on 5432; the owner chose not to run Docker now

change: dclab_rnd/tracing.py, dclab_rnd/watch_mlflow.py, scripts/watch.py, deploy/langfuse/ (new); dclab_rnd/observe.py (span name and attributes, annotate, export); models/gateway.py (span names, the request's numbers); agents/harness.py, agents/runtime.py, experience/hooks.py, jobs/worker.py (span names); agentic/server.py (the request's root span); CLAUDE.md; tests/test_trace_export.py, tests/test_watch_mlflow.py.

findings.defect: New write routes did not say what they record
findings.scenario: the admin sign-in routes were added without an entry in the write-route list
findings.cause: the experience test checks every write route names what it records
findings.fix: the three admin routes say they are audited, not steps of solving

findings.defect: The new tracing settings were not documented, and the data catalog was stale
findings.scenario: the nightly full gate: the settings test listed the five new DCLAB_ settings, and the catalog test found the generated catalog older than the code
findings.cause: the package added settings without their lines in .env.example and did not rebuild the catalog
findings.fix: the settings documented with their safe defaults; make catalog

measurements.name: the exporter against a local receiver
measurements.result: both targets receive the batch; the ids, nesting and attributes survive; a planted prompt with a table value is dropped; a sealed span is refused; a target that is down is counted
limits: not run against a real MLflow or Langfuse server yet: the owner chose not to start Docker; MLflow's OTLP endpoint is assumed from its documentation

outcome: DCLab can send every span and training to MLflow and Langfuse with one setting; it sends nothing until that setting is made.
lessons: send what already exists before adding a second tracing system: DCLab's spans had the ids, they lacked only names and an exporter
risks: MLflow's OTLP ingestion and Langfuse's attribute mapping are untested against real servers
the agent step span opens after the step has run, so its duration is not the step's
